content: Miconazole buccal tablets, commonly known by the brand name Oravig, are used to treat fungal infections in the mouth or throat. This medication belongs to the azole antifungal class of drugs. How to Use: Before using miconazole, read the patient information leaflet and instructions provided by your pharmacist. Use this medication as directed by your doctor, typically once daily in the morning after brushing your teeth. To apply the tablet: 1. Identify the area in your mouth where the tablet will be placed. It should be positioned on the upper gum, just above the left or right incisor tooth (the teeth next to your two front teeth). 2. With dry hands, place the tablet in your mouth with the rounded side facing your gum. Gently press it into place. 3. 4. Leave the tablet in place until it dissolves completely, which usually takes about 6 hours or longer. You may eat and drink while the tablet is in place, but avoid chewing gum. Do not crush, chew, or swallow the tablet. Check if the tablet is still in place after brushing your teeth, rinsing your mouth, eating, or drinking. Before applying the next dose, clear away any remaining pieces of the previous tablet. If the tablet does not stick or falls off within the first 6 hours, reapply it as directed. If it still does not adhere, replace it with a new tablet. However, if the tablet falls off or is accidentally swallowed after 6 hours, do not apply a new dose. For optimal results, continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Antifungal medications work best when the drug concentration in your body is maintained at a consistent level. Side Effects: Common side effects may include discomfort, sores, taste changes, or irritation/pain in the mouth. Other possible side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, or headache. Serious allergic reactions are rare but can occur. If you experience symptoms such as difficulty breathing, swelling, or severe rash, seek medical attention immediately. Precautions: Before using miconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as milk protein concentrate, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly needed, as there is limited data on its safety in pregnant women. It is unknown if miconazole passes into breast milk. Discuss the benefits and risks of breastfeeding while using this medication with your doctor. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
